# CV

### CV

### **TRINH HOANG NAM**

Thu Duc, Ho Chi Minh City |  |

### **PROFILE**

Embedded software engineer, eleven years, the last six of them in automotive. I write C that runs on a microcontroller with 320 KB of RAM, no operating system in the sense most engineers mean it, and a watchdog that will reset the board if my task overruns its budget by 40 milliseconds. The interesting constraint in this work is not cleverness, it is evidence: a function that is correct is worth much less than a function that is correct and can be shown to be correct to a safety assessor who does not trust me.

### **EXPERIENCE**

### **Senior Embedded Software Engineer**

Apr 2019 - Present

_Bosch Global Software Technologies Vietnam, Ho Chi Minh City_

- Body control and comfort domain for a European OEM programme. AUTOSAR Classic on Infineon AURIX TC3xx, MCAL up from the vendor, application layer ours. Team of nine in Ho Chi Minh City working against an architecture owned in Stuttgart.

- Own the door and seat control modules: window anti-pinch, mirror fold, seat memory positioning. Anti-pinch is the piece I have spent the most hours on, because the requirement is a force limit, the input is a motor current ripple signal, and the gap between those two things is where the whole engineering lives.

- Took the anti-pinch detection from a fixed-threshold implementation to a ripple-count model with temperature and battery-voltage compensation. False trips on cold-start dropped from roughly one in 90 cycles to none observed across a 5,000-cycle validation run at -20 C.

- Software unit level ISO 26262 up to ASIL-B on this module: safety requirements traced to design, design to code, code to test, all of it in a tool chain the assessor reads rather than in a document I wrote afterwards. Two assessment rounds passed without a major finding.

- MISRA C:2012 compliance across the module, deviations recorded with justification rather than suppressed. I killed about 40 of the 300 inherited deviations by changing the code instead of arguing for the exemption, which was slower and correct.

- Set up the hardware-in-the-loop regression for our domain on a dSPACE bench: 214 test cases, nightly, CAN stimulus and response checked against the requirement rather than against the previous build's behaviour. Before this we found integration defects at the OEM's vehicle test, which costs about three weeks per finding.

- Debugging is most of the job and I am unembarrassed about that: Lauterbach TRACE32, a logic analyser, and one memorable fortnight with an oscilloscope on a LIN bus that turned out to be a ground offset on a supplier's ECU and not our software at all.

- Mentor three junior engineers. The thing I teach first is reading the datasheet and the errata sheet before writing anything, because half the bugs I am asked to look at are documented silicon behaviour that nobody read.

### **Embedded Software Engineer**

Feb 2016 - Mar 2019

_Renesas Design Vietnam, Ho Chi Minh City_

- Driver and middleware development for RH850 automotive microcontrollers - CAN, SPI, ADC and timer drivers shipped as part of the vendor sample software and peripheral driver package.

- Wrote and maintained the CAN driver used by several customer evaluation projects. Being on the supplier side taught me what a driver looks like to the person who did not write it, which is the single most useful thing I have learned about interface design.

- Bring-up work on new silicon: first code running on an engineering sample, before the reference manual is finished, with an FAE in Japan on the other end of an email chain.

- Low-power modes, clock tree configuration, and the class of bug where the part wakes correctly 1,000 times and hangs on the 1,001st because of a race between the clock switch and a pending interrupt.

### **Embedded Engineer**

Aug 2014 - Jan 2016

_VNPT Technology, Ha Noi_

- Firmware and embedded Linux for consumer network devices - GPON ONT and Wi-Fi routers on Broadcom

and Realtek SoCs, OpenWrt-derived userspace.

- Board bring-up, U-Boot porting, kernel driver patches for GPIO and LED, and factory test software for the production line.

- First job. I shipped a firmware in 2015 with a memory leak in the TR-069 client that took two weeks to appear in the field; the recall of a firmware over 40,000 devices is a good early lesson in what "it works on my bench" is worth.

### **EDUCATION**

- *B.Eng, Electronics and Telecommunications** 2010 - 2014

_Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology (HCMUT)_

- GPA 8.1/10. Graduation project: a CAN-based data logger for a motorcycle engine ECU.

### **CERTIFICATIONS**

|**Certified Automotive Software Engineer, Foundation Level**|iSQI, 2020|
|---|---|
|**ISTQB Foundation Level**|2018|
|**Functional Safety - ISO 26262 for Software (internal Bosch qualification)**|2021|

### **SKILLS**

- **Languages:** C (C99 and MISRA C:2012, the language I am strongest in by a distance), C++ up to C++14 for tooling and desktop-side test harnesses, Python for test automation and log analysis, a little Rust on personal hardware and not in production

- **Architectures and silicon:** Infineon AURIX TC3xx (TriCore), Renesas RH850, ARM Cortex-M0+/M4/M7 (STM32, NXP Kinetis), Cortex-A for embedded Linux work, plus the general habits - startup code, linker scripts, memory maps, interrupt latency budgets

- **Automotive:** AUTOSAR Classic (RTE, BSW configuration, MCAL integration), CAN and CAN FD, LIN, UDS diagnostics (ISO 14229) and OBD, calibration data and A2L, Vector CANoe/CANalyzer, dSPACE hardware-in-the-loop

- **Safety and process:** ISO 26262 up to ASIL-B at the software unit and integration level, requirement traceability, static analysis (Polyspace, QA-C), code review against a checklist that an assessor will read, Automotive SPICE at the level of a practitioner rather than an assessor

- **RTOS and low-level:** OSEK/AUTOSAR OS, FreeRTOS, bare-metal superloop with a cooperative scheduler, DMA, low-power state machines, bootloaders and flash-driver-level programming

- **Linux side:** Yocto, buildroot, U-Boot, kernel character and platform drivers, device tree - current but not my deepest area since 2016

- **Tools:** Lauterbach TRACE32, Segger J-Link and Ozone, Green Hills and Tasking compilers, Git, Jenkins, oscilloscope and logic analyser, which are debugging tools and not hardware credentials

### **TWO THINGS I GOT WRONG**

The seat memory feature shipped in 2021 with a latent bug: a position stored during a low-voltage condition could be written half-updated to EEPROM, and the recovery path restored the old value without telling anyone. It was found in the field, not by us, and it was found because there was no checksum on a structure I had decided did not need one. Every persisted structure I write now carries a version byte and a CRC, and I did not learn that from a standard.

Separately, I spent most of 2020 arguing for a partial rewrite of an inherited state machine that was ugly and worked. I lost the argument, correctly. The rewrite would have consumed a requalification cycle to buy readability.

### **LANGUAGES**

Vietnamese - native. English - TOEIC 890 (2022); working language with the German and Indian sites, all review meetings and all documentation. German - A2, enough to read a supplier datasheet with a dictionary and not enough to claim.

Available on request.
